text:
Minnesota did not win this one on a hot night in goal or a lucky bounce. The Wild won it by owning the puck and the quality of the chances. They out-attempted Nashville 62 to 46 and generated 3.05 expected goals to the Predators' 1.51, which is almost exactly the 3 goals they scored. By the replay measure, MIN deserved to win 77 percent of the time.

The game was effectively set in the first period. Nick Foligno opened the scoring at 9:35 with a wrist shot, and Blake Coleman made it 2-0 on the power play at 13:48. Minnesota was ahead in expected goals in every period (1.03 to 0.60 in the first), so the lead was earned rather than borrowed. Quinn Hughes drove much of it, playing 27:30 with five shots on goal and an assist, while Minnesota controlled 1.60 expected goals to 0.55 against whenever he was on the ice.

Nashville's best moment was also its least likely one. Roman Josi cut the lead to 2-1 at 9:23 of the second with a slap shot that carried only a 4 percent chance of scoring, the sort of goal a team can't build a comeback on. Kirill Kaprizov ended any hope with a tip-in at 4:42 of the third. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 19 of 20 for Minnesota, a shade better than the 1.51 goals expected, while Juuse Saros allowed three on 30 shots, right on his expected total. Neither goalie stole anything. The skaters decided it.
